column1: # ComputerBase — Valorant mit Unreal Engine 5 im Benchmark-Test (page 2).
# Imported 2026-10-17. Figures from each bar's data-value attribute via
# src/lib/perfEngine/computerbase.js (the WQHD and UHD charts; average FPS and
# Settings, from the article's own table: "Maximale Grafikdetails, 4×MSAA" at
# 2.560 × 1.440 and 3.840 × 2.160, native (the game has no upscaler). The scene
# is a 20-second sequence on Icebox, which the article says runs at about the
# lowest frame rates in the game.
# Test system, from "Das Testsystem und die Benchmark-Szene": Ryzen 7 9800X3D
# at stock on an Asus ROG Crosshair X670E Hero (BIOS 2506); 48 GB G.Skill
# TridentZ Neo, 2 × 24 GB DDR5-6000 CL30-38-38-96; Windows 11 24H2 with HVCI on;
# ReBAR on. Drivers: AMD Adrenalin 25.6.3, Nvidia GeForce 577.00, Intel Arc 6972.
# NOT imported: GeForce RTX 3060 and Arc A770 (memory size not stated; the
# catalogue holds both variants of the 3060, and the A770 was sold as 8 GB and
# 16 GB), and the UWQHD chart (no ultrawide resolution in the model).
title:     Valorant mit Unreal Engine 5 im Benchmark-Test: Benchmarks (WQHD, UWQHD & UHD), Frametimes und VRAM
driver:    AMD Adrenalin 25.6.3; NVIDIA GeForce 577.00; Intel Arc 6972
scene:     20-second sequence on the Icebox map (described in the article)
